.._comment_prerelease: ADR-3292 (supersedes the candidate parts of ADR-1201 and ADR-1348 for the 0.x line). The release line restarts at 0.1.0: plain 0.x minors and patches, no candidates, `versioning: default` with `bump-minor-pre-major` (a feature or a breaking change on 0.x gives the next minor, a fix the next patch). Candidates return only for the first stable 1.0.0, from 1.0.0-rc.4 on: that cut sets `versioning: prerelease`, `prerelease: true` and `prerelease-type: rc` again (ADR-1348). scripts/release/check-one-shot-fields.sh requires prerelease versioning, or a release-as, while the manifest carries a candidate suffix.
.._comment_release_as: ADR-3292 / ADR-1151: one-shot. Moves the next release off the 1.0.0-rc.3 candidate line to 0.1.0 (release-please applies release-as before it reads the commits). scripts/release/rollover-changelog-fragments.sh deletes this field and this comment in the release-merge pull request; check-one-shot-fields.sh fails once the manifest is final and either survives.
.._comment_changelog_notes: GitHub generates the release body from the merged pull requests rather than from commit subjects (ADR-1233). Sections come from .github/release.yml, which groups BY LABEL -- so .github/workflows/pr-type-label.yml derives a type:* label from each PR's Conventional-Commit prefix. Without that labeler every PR falls into the catch-all: 32 of the last 40 merged PRs carried no label at all. changelog-sections below still drives CHANGELOG.md, which is rendered from changelog.d fragments, so both surfaces stay meaningful.
